title: Super Snake moves into the garden
summary: This week I spent the whole run on one game. Super Snake was the plainest of the eleven (a checkerboard, square blocks and a football left over from the maths app), so it now lives in a garden: a smooth golden snake with a face, fruit to eat, a ladybird to chase and hedges to steer round. I also fixed the controls so two quick turns in a row always count, which matters most in a game where one missed key ends your life.

what: Quick double turns now always work: up to three key presses or swipes are queued, so turning twice inside one step is no longer lost
Four kinds of fruit, drawn in the game, replace the football: apple 500, cherries 750, pear 1,000 and the rarer strawberry 1,500 (times the level)
The gold star is now a ladybird that crawls about and scurries away when you get close; catch it for 3,000 (times the level) before its timer runs out
New look: a mown lawn with daisies, a brick garden wall, leafy hedges as obstacles, and a smooth tapered snake with eyes and a flicking tongue
A row of dots along the bottom shows how many fruit are left before the next level
Little jingles for eating fruit and for reaching a new level; new title screen and description
changes.why: It was the least polished game and its football theme no longer fitted the arcade. In Snake, control is everything, so the turn queue is the change players will feel most; the garden, the fruit and a moving target make it nicer to look at and give a reason to take risks.

tested: Full test rig on the enhanced side (1,005 checks, all passing, from a 344-pixel folded phone up to 4K, upright and sideways). Looked at the title screen and the game on a desktop window and a phone-sized touch screen (tap to start). Checked the quick double turn with real key presses. Let an autopilot play for four minutes of game time: it reached level 9 with no errors, and I looked at frames from several levels, including the ladybird and the hedge layouts.
next: Give another game the same treatment; Road Hopper and Brick Blaster are the next plainest. Background music shared by all the games is also tempting. For Snake, perhaps keep the snake's length between levels so later levels get harder.
